findings.issue_text: P1, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-165` — `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` / `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` — Uses the caller’s calendar credentials instead of the booking organizer’s; attendee/team callers may update the wrong calendar or fail.

P1, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-106,165` — `await prisma.booking.update(...)` precedes `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` — A calendar failure leaves persisted guests but reports failure; retries reject the already-added guests, permanently desynchronizing the calendar.

P1, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:3-6`; `addGuests.handler.ts:74-78,100-103` — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` — Input is neither uniqueness-constrained nor deduplicated; duplicate or concurrent requests can create duplicate attendees or fail through a check-then-insert race.

P2, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:166` — `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` — Passes unfiltered input instead of `uniqueGuests`; existing attendees included in mixed requests are misclassified as newly added and receive the wrong email.

P1, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5` — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` — No cardinality limit permits attendee-row bloat and unbounded calendar/email fan-out, enabling authenticated resource exhaustion.

P1, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-78` — `map((email) => email.toLowerCase())` with `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` — Guest input and existing attendee addresses are not normalized; mixed-case variants bypass the denylist and duplicate-attendee detection.

P1, confidence 75 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:50-56` — `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` — Any attendee can mutate the organizer’s attendee list and disclose meeting details, including video credentials, to arbitrary recipients.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-165` — `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` / `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` — Uses the caller’s calendar credentials instead of the booking organizer’s; attendee/team callers may update the wrong calendar or fail.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts, lines 158-165 show: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });`. The `ctx.user` is the caller (the person making the API request), not necessarily the booking organizer. The booking organizer is stored in `booking.user` or `organizer`. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, they would be using their own calendar credentials to update the calendar event, not the organizer's credentials. This is a real bug - the calendar update should use the organizer's credentials (booking.user.credentials which is already fetched in the booking query) to properly update the calendar event on the organizer's calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-106,165` — `await prisma.booking.update(...)` precedes `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` — A calendar failure leaves persisted guests but reports failure; retries reject the already-added guests, permanently desynchronizing the calendar.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real consistency issue. Looking at the code flow in addGuests.handler.ts: 1) Lines 92-106 update the database with new guests via prisma.booking.update(), 2) Line 165 calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees() to sync with external calendars. If the calendar update fails, the database already has the guests persisted. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) will exclude the already-added guests since they're now in booking.attendees, causing the retry to fail with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. This creates a permanent desync where guests exist in the database but not in the calendar, with no way to retry the calendar sync. This is a real transactional consistency bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1, confidence 100 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5` — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` — No cardinality limit permits attendee-row bloat and unbounded calendar/email fan-out, enabling authenticated resource exhaustion.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the ZAddGuestsInputSchema at line 5 of addGuests.schema.ts defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` without any maximum length constraint. Looking at the handler in addGuests.handler.ts, this array is used to: 1) create database records via `createMany` for each guest, 2) send emails to all attendees via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, and 3) update calendar attendees via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`. An authenticated user could pass thousands of email addresses in a single request, causing database bloat, excessive email sending, and calendar API abuse. This is a legitimate resource exhaustion vulnerability - there's no `.max()` constraint on the array to limit the number of guests that can be added in a single request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1, confidence 75 — `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:50-56` — `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` — Any attendee can mutate the organizer’s attendee list and disclose meeting details, including video credentials, to arbitrary recipients.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at lines 50-56 allows any attendee of a booking to add guests. Looking at the authorization logic: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` - this means if ANY of these conditions is true, the user can proceed. An attendee (someone who was invited to the meeting) can therefore add arbitrary new guests to the booking, which will: 1) Add them to the database, 2) Update calendar events via EventManager, 3) Send emails with meeting details including video call credentials. This is a legitimate security concern - attendees typically shouldn't have the authority to invite additional people to meetings without organizer approval. The video call data including passwords is included in the CalendarEvent and sent to new guests. This represents a real authorization/permission issue where the permission model may be too permissive.
